questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that i got to go there with friends, in addition to the great reputation University of Milan has as a destination for exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When helping each other along the way, we found it quite easy to source the information on how to get formalities done upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received a lot of emails from Unimi. In addition to this, particularly Massimo was very friendly, and was always ready to answer questions if we had any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find housing. However, we started the process of finding housing a year prior to our arrival. It is quite expensive in Milan, but you can find apartments quite close to University.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is the absolute go-to. I have not heard of anyone living on campus in Milan, but living off campus was a great experience, that made us see so much of the wonderful city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Coming from UCPH, it can be quite confusing to register for courses. The concept is totally different that in Copenhagen, and not at all as formal and rigid.

However, it takes some getting used to.

Generally, you have to just try out the courses without registering it anywhere. When you have then settled for a course, you enter Unimi's students portal and register for the course there. You have to remember, to register for the exam at the end of the course also.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Many of the professors were very willing to explain in detail how it is done, when you initially are trying out their courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy, and I got every course that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Accept the lack of familities that you may be used to from a university back home, and ask the polite professors in order to get a grasp of the concept.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I feel like the level of courses was somewhat lower that what I am used to as a student from UCPH. However, it is also a very different learning approach, and in many classes you are not expected to read much literature.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
First of all, there were many more class sessions, and you are required to attend these. Second of all there was not much reading.

In conclusion, to get a grasp of each course, you had to sit down at the class sessions and learn from the professors directly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Criminal Law
Labour Law and Environmental Sustainability
Scientific Innovation and Legal Challenges of Food Regulation
Comparative Contract Law
International Organizations and Sustainable Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially Comparative Contract Law, and Labour Law and Environmental Sustainability was a joy for me.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not many.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than back home. However, we spent a lot of money on trips, tickets and eating out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an ERASMUS-organization that welcomed us.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take time and weekends off to go on trips around Milan - Florence, Como, Bologna etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a lot of trips around Italy!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, and very joyful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was a certain language barrier. Furthermore, people did not seem as busy, as they may seem in Denmark, and that may be a little irritating when you yourself are in a hurry. But my best advice is to settle down, lower you shoulders and follow the rhythm.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really came to appreciate the laissez faire-lifestyle in the end.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It is going to be more expensive, that you think. So save up, and boost the "unexpected expenses" part of your budget.
Take it easy upon arrival, and feel your way around the university. Get a feel for how they do things compared to UCPH.
Remember to enjoy the city, the surroundings and all the other exchange-students!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends, and getting all of those experiences that you would never get, if you just were to go to Italy on vacation!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not many, really.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
